body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Party banter for one act: nine short exchanges between companions, spoken as the party walks about the Hollow. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies in banter. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW BANTER WORKS. While the party explores, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between two or three companions who happen to be in the party, once each, on entering an area. The area is unknown: write chat that could happen anywhere on a walk (the weather, the night, food, rest, habits, each other's quirks, the Express, the moon, the road, old trades and old manners). Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else, and needs no setup. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more.

ACT THREE. The last stretch: whatever is coming is close and everyone knows it. They are tired and fond of each other and say so sideways, through jokes and small gestures; gallows humour, with one honest line now and then. Name no place and no event except the Hollow in general, the Crooked House and the Express's crash.

BANTER RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; a trio may let the third speak last or interrupt. Every speaker in the list speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached voice sheets and fact lists, plus the pairing seeds. Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters beyond those named. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic; no line may repeat a line in a voice sheet.
3. Pet phrases: each at most once in the whole reply. Companions call each other by first name unless their voice sheet says otherwise.
4. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.

THE NINE EXCHANGES (in this order; the topic of each is yours, chosen from the seeds and facts):
EXCHANGE 1: Delphine + Lucan (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, lucan_houndstooth)
EXCHANGE 2: Silas + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, cordelia_skein)
EXCHANGE 3: Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
EXCHANGE 4: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
EXCHANGE 5: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
EXCHANGE 6: Rook + Tobin (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward)
EXCHANGE 7: Silas + Lucan (speaker ids: silas_vane, lucan_houndstooth)
EXCHANGE 8: Rook + Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
EXCHANGE 9: Silas + Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)

PAIRING SEEDS (optional starting points, from the characters' files; use a seed at most once, and a pair listed twice must not reuse one):
- Delphine and Lucan: an old-fashioned showwoman and an old-fashioned gentleman of the hunt trade manners and billing; Your Foolishness and the hound.
- Silas and Cordelia: a skeleton who reads a room by his rattle meets a woman who reads a room by pulses; ribs and viscosity.
- Tobin and Silas: a friction pair turning to friends: Tobin freezes near Silas's flint lighter and his censer, Silas hauls a bucket past him; Silas's fake tonics, Tobin's diagnoses.
- Rook and Lucan: the ghost hound sits on Rook's armoured boot and yips; Rook deadpans that an unlicensed phantom mastiff breaks three municipal leash statutes; Lucan insists the hound has sensed a doom-laden draught.
- Delphine and Cordelia: tailoring and seams: Delphine eyes Cordelia's eight-sleeved waistcoat; Cordelia admires Delphine's stitching; two women who made themselves something other than what they were made as. Light and funny only.
- Rook and Tobin: Rook plants his shield between Tobin and a smouldering ember; Tobin asks why a grave-guard cares about straw and twine; Rook says a watchman counts everyone on the parish roll, in bone or burlap.
- Silas and Lucan: a gambler and a hunter: odds against grades out of ten; the hound and the shadow; Lucan corrects Silas's grammar.
- Tobin and Lucan: Lucan sniffs Tobin's straw and woodsmoke and scores the bouquet nine out of ten for rustic comfort; the hound never chews Tobin's hem.
- Silas and Delphine: thick as thieves: a three-card monte and a shared contempt for the house; they compare the fine print on their leashes.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly nine EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 9, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY delphine_ravelle: Your spectral hound is staring at my hem again, darling, and Your Foolishness is offering three-to-one odds he chews the velvet before we reach the Crooked House.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Barnaby would never savage a lady's wardrobe, Delphine, though I fear my own manners are wearing rather thin at the edges tonight.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Nonsense, you still bow like a headliner before every ambush, even when the cheap seats are throwing teeth at us.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: One keeps up the old courtesies, if you please, because when a gentleman forgets how to bow, the yellow in his eyes takes over the whole posture.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Then I shall keep calling your cue from the wings, darling, until the last curtain comes down on this whole miserable valley.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY cordelia_skein: The wind through your ribs has pitched up a full third since the last milepost, Silas, which suggests an acute spike in anticipation or dread.
SAY silas_vane: Tell's in the twitch, friend, not the ribcage, and a smart player always lets the house think his nerve is fraying before he turns the last card.
SAY cordelia_skein: You have no pulse for me to chart, darling, yet you have been shuffling those bone slivers at double your baseline ratio for the past hour.
SAY silas_vane: Look, when you can see the roof of the Crooked House over the ridge, you either keep your hands moving or you start counting what you owe.
SAY cordelia_skein: If my hands begin to tremble before the final assay, you have my full permission to mock my calibration.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep that brass censer on your windward flank, Silas, my burlap is bone-dry and I have no wish to go up like a beacon before the finish.
SAY silas_vane: Relax, friend, I banked the bitter herbs an hour back and I've been hauling this leaky bucket of ditch water three paces behind you just in case.
SAY tobin_hayward: You carried a bucket of ditch water up a mud trail with your knuckles split and never even tried to charge me a copper for it?
SAY silas_vane: Don't go getting misty about it, you old sack of hay, I just need someone left standing to tell me my pulse is skipping when we're done.
SAY tobin_hayward: You haven't got a pulse in those ribs, you daft fraud, though your collar seam is holding together better than most.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY rook_coldwake: Your phantom hound is parked square on my greave again, Lucan, which breaks three separate municipal leash statutes even in an unincorporated hollow.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Do forgive him, Rook, he only seeks out cold iron when he scents a particularly foul draught rolling down from the ridge.
SAY rook_coldwake: Either it is a doom-laden draught or I dropped a crust of kettle corn in my boot cuff before we marched.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, he has no eye for dignity tonight, though I confess it eases my mind to walk beside someone whose shield never wavers.
SAY rook_coldwake: Settle down now, the Watch does not abandon a post just because the neighbours have poor posture.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY delphine_ravelle: Eight sleeves cut on the bias, darling, and not a single pucker at the shoulder seam, whoever fitted that charcoal silk deserves top billing.
SAY cordelia_skein: And your cuff repairs are remarkably neat, Delphine, considering you stitched them mid-stride with a needle that looks suited for sailcloth.
SAY delphine_ravelle: A girl has to keep her stuffing tucked in when the road gets rough, or the critics start calling the whole act threadbare.
SAY cordelia_skein: Quite right, darling, if we are to dissect whatever waits at the end of this lane, we ought to arrive with impeccable tailoring.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY tobin_hayward: You just planted a coffin-lid shield between my boots and a drift of hot cinders, Rook, and you didn't even break step to do it.
SAY rook_coldwake: Unattended embers on a public footway are a clear zoning hazard, Tobin, and dry straw catches faster than damp bone.
SAY tobin_hayward: Most watchmen wouldn't count a bundle of old twine and field mice as worth scorching their brass knocker over.
SAY rook_coldwake: If you walked out of the Express's crash with us, you are on my shift log, and nobody on my shift log burns while I can lift a slab.
SAY tobin_hayward: Hold still when we make camp tonight, then, because the leather strap on your shield arm is fraying right through.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY silas_vane: Ten to one the next ugly thing out of the brush lunges for the lantern first, Lucan, care to put a silver piece on the table?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: A gentleman does not wager on the quarry, Silas, though based on the sloppy spoor in this mud, I cannot award it higher than a four out of ten.
SAY silas_vane: Four out of ten is generous when my own shadow is hugging my heels tighter than your ghost dog.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: One says "tighter than your hound does", if you please, though I admit the dark ahead has teeth enough to rattle any man's grammar.
SAY silas_vane: Stick close to my left rib when we hit the door, friend, and we'll see whose manners hold out longer.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY lucan_houndstooth: The air off the Hollow tastes of rusted iron and wet cellar stone tonight, friends, a prime specimen of bad weather.
SAY rook_coldwake: Subsoil drainage has given out altogether along this stretch, and my fingers are going soft as river mud in the damp.
SAY tobin_hayward: Rub your grave-wax into the knuckles before the chill sets deeper, Rook, and Lucan, stop sniffing the blight like it's vintage cider.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: One must catalogue the bouquet of the night, Tobin, especially when your own turnip lantern and dry straw remain a steady nine out of ten for comfort.
SAY rook_coldwake: Keep that lantern three paces clear of his cuffs all the same, we have one more docket to clear before we rest.

EXCHANGE 9
SAY silas_vane: Look at the crone on that moon tonight, grinning down like she holds every marked card in the shoe and knows our tabs are due.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Let her grin, darling, Your Foolishness has been whispering terrible riddles about her all evening and I intend to spoil her final act.
SAY cordelia_skein: If both of you intend to spit in the eye of local pathology, do keep your voices steady so my silk notes do not dissolve prematurely.
SAY silas_vane: House always wins, unless you burn the house, and I couldn't ask for better company to strike the match.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, we are walking out of that Crooked House together even if Cordelia has to stitch us back up by hand.
